items.parsed_text: Handysize/Supramax Report10th April 2026 63,500 Atlantic: FIRMER Paciﬁc: FIRMER 38,000 Atlantic: FLAT Paciﬁc: FLAT Atlantic Comment The Baltic Dry Index (BDI) reached 2,095 points this week, marking a cautious recovery as the market began pricing in a fragile two-week ceaseﬁre in the Middle East. While the news of the Strait of Hormuz potentially reopening via alternative routes oﬀered some psychological relief, bunker volatility remains extreme. This spike in costs has kept voyage rates artiﬁcially high, particularly for Capesize vessels in the Paciﬁc, even as actual demand from Chinese steel mills remains soft. Meanwhile, the South Atlantic continues to carry the market's heavy lifting, with Brazil’s soybean harvest now over 80% complete and a record 178-million-tonne crop ﬂooding export terminals, ensuring a steady stream of cargo that is keeping vessel supply tight despite the high cost of fuel. On the Continent, the market has remained muted, with minimal cargo enquiry continuing the trend seen last week. On the Handysize market, owners are rating Trans-Atlantic trips on large Handys at around USD 17,000, though we have yet to see these levels translate into ﬁxtures. On the Supramax and Ultramax market, we saw a 61,000 deadweight vessel ﬁx basis Antwerp for a trip to Turkey with steels at USD 17,000, in line with levels seen last week, indicating a largely ﬂat market. In the Mediterranean, the Handysize market saw very little activity, with sentiment remaining largely positional, highlighted by the lack of reported ﬁxtures. Indicatively, we saw a 35,000 deadweight vessel ﬁx basis Saﬁ for a short trip to South Spain at USD 8,500. On the Supramax and Ultramax market, Trans-Atlantic trips are continuing to ﬁx at around USD 10,000. We saw a 60,000 deadweight vessel ﬁx basis Yesilovacik for a trip to redeliver in Brownsville at USD 10,000 for 50 days, although the split for the balance is unknown. The East Coast South America (ECSA) Handysize market has shown renewed strength this week, with the supply-demand balance tipping back in favor of owners. This ﬁrming sentiment was clearly highlighted by a recent ﬁxture where a large eco Handysize secured $20,000 for a trip from Recalada to the West Mediterranean. While other Atlantic regions have seen more modest movements, the ECSA basin continues to lead the way, with owners successfully leveraging the steady ﬂow of fresh inquiries to push rates back toward the psychological $20,000 threshold. Despite a ﬂurry of activity for Supramax and Ultramax ECSA routes this week, the market has essentially moved sideways as the industry navigates a condensed trading window. The short work week between the Christian Easter and the upcoming Orthodox Easter have created a sense of urgency among charterers to cover prompt requirements, yet this uptick in inquiries has failed to translate into signiﬁcant rate gains. On the USG Handysize market, the week began on a quiet note due to the Monday holiday across most markets, with sentiment initially weighed down by softer rate levels carried over from last week. As activity resumed, we saw a bit more activity and rates showing some slight improvement, with sentiment picking up a touch as the week progressed. Owners are showing a bit more conﬁdence looking ahead to next week, expecting the market to ﬁrm further. However, underlying fundamentals remain somewhat unbalanced, with the tonnage list still longer than the available cargo volume, limiting stronger upward momentum. The Supramax and Ultramax market has continued to improve throughout the week, with Trans-Atlantic trips on Ultramaxes now ﬁxing in the USD 20,000s. The remaining tonnage count for the month appears well balanced against the inﬂux of fresh cargo enquiries seen over the course of the week. For front-haul petcoke business, owners are now holding levels closer to USD 25,000, representing a signiﬁcant increase of around USD 6,000 compared to last week, where similar ﬁxtures were concluded closer to USD 19,000. The brief reopening of the Strait of Hormuz led to a temporary easing in bunker prices and a rise in FFA levels; however, the subsequent closure quickly reintroduced uncertainty to both trade ﬂows and cost expectations. Against this backdrop, the market was characterised by a strong period segment, ﬁrm spot support, and increasingly bullish owner sentiment. The Indonesian coal sector showed signs of recovery, with an uptick in fresh cargoes and a noticeable drawdown of prompt tonnage, leading to some improvement in regional balance. On the Indo/Seasia route, heard one UMX open Phils ﬁxed USD 19k for Indo/Phils; on Indo/China, levels also ﬁrmed, with heard one UMX open Singapore ﬁxed USD 17k and another SMX open KSC ﬁxed USD 12.5k. The Indo/India (WCI) market remained well supported in terms of levels, although reported ﬁxtures were limited, including heard one UMX del Cai Mei ﬁxed USD 19k, suggesting owners are still testing higher. The North Vietnam / South China region continued to act as a key driver of the basin. Clinker exports from Vietnam to Bdesh remained strong, with heard one SMX open S.China ﬁxed USD 20k. Additional ﬂows to West Africa were also noted, including heard one UMX open Chaozhou ﬁxed USD 16,500 with split days. Bulk cement shipments to the USG were likewise active, with heard one UMX open Cambodia ﬁxed USD 15.5k split. Meanwhile, the start of the nickel ore season has supported activity, with heard one SMX open Xiamen ﬁxed USD 16k for nickel ore to North China. The NOPAC market remained relatively stable, though activity was limited. Owners are currently oﬀering around USD 18k for a NOPAC round, while charterers’ bids remain closer to USD 16k, leaving a noticeable gap and resulting in limited deal ﬂow. In North China, steel and general cargo exports softened slightly in terms of activity, with fewer ﬁxtures reported. Bulk cargoes, however, continued to provide support, including heard one SMX open N.China ﬁxed USD 18k for a trip to Sri Lanka and another UMX ﬁxed at similar levels for BOP. The slag to Bdesh trade remained particularly ﬁrm, with UMX still achieving USD 20k+. The Australia market also maintained a ﬁrm tone, with steady cargo ﬂows across grains, salt, coal and ore. Heard one UMX open Gresik ﬁxed USD 19k for Aus/Phils grains, and another UMX open ECI ﬁxed USD 14k dop for Aus/China grains, reﬂecting continued support in the basin. The period market remained strong, underpinned by both ﬁrm spot sentiment and FFA support. UMX short period ﬁxtures were commonly concluded around USD 19k, while one-year deals held at approximately USD 17k–17.5k+, indicating sustained owner conﬁdence in the near-term outlook. Overall, the Paciﬁc Supramax market maintained a ﬁrm and slightly strengthening tone this week. With continued cargo ﬂow and strong owner resistance, the market is likely to remain well supported in the short term, with potential for further upside —let’s see next week! items.parsed_text: Panam ax/Kam sarm ax Report10th April 2026 ATL: FIRMER PAC: FIRMER MID EAST: FIRMER Market Comments ATL SHORT: MARKET OUTLOOK - SUBJECT TO NO UNEXPECTED GEOPOLITICAL DEVELOPMENTS IN THE MIDDLE EAST OVER THE WEEKEND, THE OUTLOOK FOR FRONT HAUL ACTIVITY REMAINS SUPPORTIVE. IF WE SEE STRENGTHENING GRAIN DEMAND EX ECSA AND SUSTAINED ACTIVITY FROM NCSA, IT SHOULD PROVIDE SUFFICIENT SUPPORT FOR OWNERS TO MAINTAIN OR INCREASE CURRENT OFFER LEVELS PAC SHORT: THIS WEEK WAS A SLOW BURN WITH MOST OF THE SHIPPING WORLD STILL OFF FOR MONDAY DUE TO VARIOUS HOLIDAYS. DEMAND OPENEND SOLID FOR BOTH NOPAC AND INDO WHICH REMAINED A CONSISTENT THEME THROUGHOUT THE WEEK. THE HESITANT FLOOR FOUND AT THE END OF LAST WEEK CONTINUED WITH NOPAC SPREADS STARTING THE WEEK AROUND LOW 15’S VS LOW 16’S BKI CJK. Activity was slow to pick up until the Dampier major looked to secure their C5 stem for 26-28 April in line with yesterday’s ﬁxtures. A bid at $11.70 was seen against $12.10 oﬀered before ﬁxing at $11.95. One major out of Hedland ﬁxed their C5 stem at $12.15 for 23 April and rumored to have taken a Newcastlemax too . A lot of tonnage was cleared after a ﬂurry of early/mid May C3 stems were ﬁxed yesterday afternoon with many reported to be in the very low $30s. Regardless of yesterdays strong volumes - one German operator ﬁxed their 08/12 cargo early doors at $30.15 C3 while a trader also concluded for 05 May onwards at the same level. Tonnage remains long as demand is moderate. Activity blossomed in the North Atlantic yesterday afternoon as three fronthaul stems were seen to ﬁx in quick succession. A miner concluded the day, securing their stem out of Seven Islands to Oita for 01-07 May at $35.60 which out of Rotterdam ran to $53,500 for a 79 day duration or a $1.65 mil score and $58,000 when run back to c9 duration. Into Tuesday, activity resumed out of West Australia as two majors were accompanied by strong operator C5 interest. Early bids at mid/high $11.00s were not enough to tempt the mid $12's oﬀers, resulting in concession on the bid and the Dampier major taking a handful of vessels at $12.25 for 21–23 April. Building in volume, activity picked up mid-week with three majors present. Rates however fell marginally, a reﬂection primarily of the sizable drop in oil price the previous evening. Oﬀers readily lined up at mid $12.00s. That day, a Dampier and a Hedland major each took a few at $12.15 with the Dampier major covering 22–24 and 24–26 April while the Hedland major ﬁxed one earlier at $12.00. On the peripheral, a vessel ﬁxed from 11 April onwards for a TCT via Newcastle redelivery China at $22,000, whilst an operator concluded their Newcastle to Mailiao stem for 01/10 May at high $16.00’s. Volumes remained healthy through Thursday, although the trajectory of rates continued. Again oﬀers optimistically congregated at $12.50 against bids at $11.60. With a further removal of support from the bunker price, the Dampier major ﬁxed a handful at $11.85 C5. Operators bid the same levels on the follow, eager to capitalise on the softer oﬀers. prompting other operators to bid at similar levels. On he peripheral, the usual Teluk operator ﬁxed a stem to Dung Quat for 20–22 April with the last bid seen around $7.00. Sentiment clearly positive in the East rolling into the ﬁnal day of the week. With most of Europe relaxing on Monday, the South did not ﬁnd rythm until mid-week. With a solid cargo book and owner's ambition still to remain within the $30's C3, Tuesday got oﬀ to a slow start. An Ubu to Gwangyang tender concluded for 08– 17 May at mid $30s C3, oﬀering initial glimpses this ambition could be achieved and even built upon. In addition, a Newcastlemax ﬁxed at $30 C3 for 06–10 May. Bids were initially stand-oﬃsh on Wednesday, as charterers watched oil prices fall. Building in activity eventually into the afternoon, where an operator's stem for 10/11 May dates ﬁxed at $30, whilst a C17 concluded for 21–30 April at $21.85. A less frequent and forward Uruguay stem similarly concluded at $32.75. Counter balancing the softer bunkers was a steady inﬂow of end April and early May cargoes, which eventually culminated in a robust cargo book. Thursday saw the height of activity and where the basin created it's ﬂoor. Owners moved oﬀ their initial $31 C3 ideas as two Newcastlemaxes ﬁxed at $29.50 and high $29s C3, setting the tone. An array of rates from $30 to $30.50 C3 were then ﬁxed for 01-10 May dates on both capes and larger tonnage. This window now felt thinner on the tonnage, aided by a further few stems being marketed that night. Come Friday, two standard capes were ﬁxed for early May at $30.15. Fronthaul business, albeit the bulk of which forward, steadily rebalanced fundamentals in the North through the ﬁrst half of the week. Tonnage however similarly light on the front end, as several vessel set their sights on West African business away from the lackluster North last week. Continuing said trend, an end user ﬁxed a North continent ship for their Buchanan lift at $28.85 for split dates. Out of Gibraltar, this ran to $57,000 for the duration and a score of $1.5m. Adjusted to C9 it was equivalent to a healthy $56,300. With plenty of attractive fronthaul business available by Thursday, volumes spiked. First, an interesting $57,500 for 76 days duration on a Newcastlemax with some additional legs at a lower rate. The second a double discharge cargo to Taiwan that ﬁxed at $34.50. Adjusted to C9 ran to $56,300 or a $1.52 m score. Finally, late that evening a miner concluded their Seven Islands to Oita for 01-07 May at $35.60 which out of Rotterdam ran to $58,000 C9 adjusted or score of $1.65 mil score. Left for Friday was a few pieces of backhaul business and a smaller fronthaul stem, against only four marketed vessels open for the remainder of April. Undoubtedly an interesting backdrop for the North to open with next week.
